findings.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — On a Storage.Create failure the code calls `recordLegacyDuration(true,...)` instead of `recordStorageDuration`, so real Storage errors are misfiled into the Legacy-failure metric, corrupting the only alerting signal operators have for detecting genuine async Legacy divergence.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129 — Same mislabeling bug in Update: a Storage.Update failure is recorded via `recordLegacyDuration(true,...)` instead of `recordStorageDuration`, further polluting the dashboard/alert that is supposed to be the only visibility into silent Legacy divergence.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — In the DeleteCollection goroutine, a genuine Legacy.DeleteCollection failure is recorded via `recordStorageDuration` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`, meaning real async Legacy-side failures never increment the Legacy error metric — the one supposed "gate" for catching silent divergence silently passes.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:139 — Update() now passes the same rest.UpdatedObjectInfo (objInfo) to both Storage.Update (sync) and Legacy.Update (async goroutine); each store independently calls objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old) against its own "old" object, so a patch/merge-style update can resolve to two different final objects in Storage vs Legacy instead of the previous pattern (removed updateWrapper) that computed the result once and applied the identical resolved object to both stores

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 — Legacy write side-effects for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection moved from synchronous best-effort calls to fire-and-forget goroutines with a 10s timeout and swallowed errors, so callers now receive a success response before (or without ever knowing whether) the legacy store write completes — weakens the timing guarantee any external consumer of the legacy store (other services, migrations, rollback to a lower DualWriterMode) implicitly relied on

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:69 — Get() now forwards the caller-supplied metav1.GetOptions (e.g. ResourceVersion) to Storage.Get instead of always using a fresh empty GetOptions; this is likely a correctness fix but changes observable behavior for clients that pass ResourceVersion (e.g. "get at cached/last-known RV" semantics used by some controllers), and is not covered by a corresponding test asserting RV-aware Get semantics for Mode3

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:79 — List() goes from an always-broken stub (nil, nil with no error, silently satisfying every LIST request with an empty non-error response) to a real implementation delegating to Storage.List; this is the first real LIST contract exposed for Mode3 resources (pagination/continue tokens, resourceVersion consistency, watch bookmarks) and has no dedicated test asserting list/continuation semantics beyond the new integration test's default doPlaylistTests coverage

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:126 — Update() no longer pre-fetches the object from Storage.Get before calling Storage.Update; if the object doesn't exist and forceAllowCreate is honored downstream, PUT-style updates may now implicitly create the resource where the old code explicitly failed with "could not get object to update" — behavior now depends entirely on Storage.Update's own semantics rather than an explicit check in this layer
pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Create's storage-failure path calls d.recordLegacyDuration instead of d.recordStorageDuration, mislabeling a Storage error as a Legacy metric
pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129 — Update's storage-failure path calls d.recordLegacyDuration instead of d.recordStorageDuration, mislabeling a Storage error as a Legacy metric

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — DeleteCollection's background Legacy.DeleteCollection call records the result via d.recordStorageDuration instead of d.recordLegacyDuration, mislabeling a Legacy metric as Storage

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — On a Storage.Create failure the code calls `recordLegacyDuration(true,...)` instead of `recordStorageDuration`, so real Storage errors are misfiled into the Legacy-failure metric, corrupting the only alerting signal operators have for detecting genuine async Legacy divergence.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Create`, the storage write is timed with `startStorage := time.Now()`, but on `d.Storage.Create(...)` error the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` instead of `recordStorageDuration(...)` (see the `if err != nil { ... }` block). This misattributes Storage failures to the Legacy metric path and uses a storage-start timestamp for a legacy metric, corrupting metrics/alerting signals.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129 — Same mislabeling bug in Update: a Storage.Update failure is recorded via `recordLegacyDuration(true,...)` instead of `recordStorageDuration`, further polluting the dashboard/alert that is supposed to be the only visibility into silent Legacy divergence.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.Update`, the Storage.Update call is timed with `startStorage := time.Now()`, but on error it invokes `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` instead of recording a storage duration (e.g., `recordStorageDuration`). This misattributes a unified-store failure to the legacy metrics, matching the finding and causing incorrect dashboard/alert data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — In the DeleteCollection goroutine, a genuine Legacy.DeleteCollection failure is recorded via `recordStorageDuration` instead of `recordLegacyDuration`, meaning real async Legacy-side failures never increment the Legacy error metric — the one supposed "gate" for catching silent divergence silently passes.

adjudication.rationale: In `DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection`, the async legacy write path uses the wrong metric recorder: inside the goroutine it does `_, err := d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)` and then calls `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` instead of `recordLegacyDuration(...)`. This misattributes legacy failures to storage metrics and prevents legacy error metrics from reflecting real async failures, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:139 — Update() now passes the same rest.UpdatedObjectInfo (objInfo) to both Storage.Update (sync) and Legacy.Update (async goroutine); each store independently calls objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old) against its own "old" object, so a patch/merge-style update can resolve to two different final objects in Storage vs Legacy instead of the previous pattern (removed updateWrapper) that computed the result once and applied the identical resolved object to both stores

adjudication.rationale: In dualwriter_mode3.go, Update() was changed from computing the updated object once (via objInfo.UpdatedObject on the Storage “old” object) and then using an updateWrapper to apply the exact resolved object to both stores, to instead calling Storage.Update(ctx, ..., objInfo, ...) synchronously and Legacy.Update(ctx, ..., objInfo, ...) asynchronously with the same rest.UpdatedObjectInfo. Since each store’s Update implementation may invoke objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old) against its own "old" state, this can resolve to different final objects in Storage vs Legacy (especially for merge/patch-style updates), whereas the previous code explicitly prevented that divergence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 — Legacy write side-effects for Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection moved from synchronous best-effort calls to fire-and-forget goroutines with a 10s timeout and swallowed errors, so callers now receive a success response before (or without ever knowing whether) the legacy store write completes — weakens the timing guarantee any external consumer of the legacy store (other services, migrations, rollback to a lower DualWriterMode) implicitly relied on

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Mode3’s legacy-side writes are now executed asynchronously and their errors are not returned to the caller: Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection call the unified store synchronously, then start a `go func()` that performs `d.Legacy.*` with `context.WithTimeoutCause(..., 10s, ...)` and only records metrics (`d.recordLegacyDuration(...)`) without propagating (or even logging) failures. This is a real, diff-grounded semantic change (callers can see success before legacy write completes/fails), but the claim about external consumers implicitly relying on the prior timing guarantee is speculative and not provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:69 — Get() now forwards the caller-supplied metav1.GetOptions (e.g. ResourceVersion) to Storage.Get instead of always using a fresh empty GetOptions; this is likely a correctness fix but changes observable behavior for clients that pass ResourceVersion (e.g. "get at cached/last-known RV" semantics used by some controllers), and is not covered by a corresponding test asserting RV-aware Get semantics for Mode3

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows DualWriterMode3.Get changed from `d.Storage.Get(ctx, name, &metav1.GetOptions{})` to `d.Storage.Get(ctx, name, options)`, so caller-supplied GetOptions (including ResourceVersion) are now forwarded, which is an observable behavior change. The added/updated Mode3 Get test (`TestMode3_Get`) only passes an empty `&metav1.GetOptions{}` and asserts the returned object, but does not assert that non-empty options (e.g., ResourceVersion) are propagated to the storage layer or affect semantics. That makes the finding about lack of RV-aware test coverage diff-grounded and actionable, but not itself a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:79 — List() goes from an always-broken stub (nil, nil with no error, silently satisfying every LIST request with an empty non-error response) to a real implementation delegating to Storage.List; this is the first real LIST contract exposed for Mode3 resources (pagination/continue tokens, resourceVersion consistency, watch bookmarks) and has no dedicated test asserting list/continuation semantics beyond the new integration test's default doPlaylistTests coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces the prior Mode3 List() stub (which logged "List not implemented" and returned (nil, nil)) with a real implementation that delegates to d.Storage.List and records metrics. While the PR adds a new unit test (TestMode3_List) and integration playlist tests exercising Mode3, the new tests only validate basic success/error behavior and do not cover any list-specific option/contract semantics (e.g., continue tokens/resourceVersion handling) beyond whatever the downstream Storage mock/integration defaults do. That’s a specific, change-driven test/coverage gap rather than a directly verifiable correctness defect in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:126 — Update() no longer pre-fetches the object from Storage.Get before calling Storage.Update; if the object doesn't exist and forceAllowCreate is honored downstream, PUT-style updates may now implicitly create the resource where the old code explicitly failed with "could not get object to update" — behavior now depends entirely on Storage.Update's own semantics rather than an explicit check in this layer

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Update() in pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go no longer calls d.Storage.Get(...) before d.Storage.Update(...). Previously, a missing object would cause an early failure at the Get step ("could not get object to update"), regardless of forceAllowCreate. Now, whether an update on a non-existent object results in an error or an implicit create depends entirely on Storage.Update’s semantics and forceAllowCreate. That is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change, but the diff alone doesn’t establish it as an incorrect defect (it may be intended to honor forceAllowCreate downstream).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 — Create's storage-failure path calls d.recordLegacyDuration instead of d.recordStorageDuration, mislabeling a Storage error as a Legacy metric

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, Create() measures the Storage.Create call with startStorage := time.Now(). On the Storage error path it calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage), which records the failure under the legacy metric even though the failure occurred in Storage. The success path correctly calls d.recordStorageDuration(..., startStorage). This is a concrete, verifiable mislabeling/incorrect metric recording introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:129 — Update's storage-failure path calls d.recordLegacyDuration instead of d.recordStorageDuration, mislabeling a Storage error as a Legacy metric

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go, DualWriterMode3.Update() measures the Storage.Update() call with startStorage := time.Now(), but in the error path it calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) instead of recording a storage duration. This misattributes a storage failure/latency to the legacy metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:166 — DeleteCollection's background Legacy.DeleteCollection call records the result via d.recordStorageDuration instead of d.recordLegacyDuration, mislabeling a Legacy metric as Storage

adjudication.rationale:
In `DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection`, the async legacy delete path calls `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)` but then records the duration with `d.recordStorageDuration(...)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration(...)`:

```go
_, err := d.Legacy.DeleteCollection(...)
d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)
```

This misattributes a Legacy operation’s metric as a Storage metric, matching the finding.
